topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: The rain's still coming down in sheets, like it's trying to wash away more than just the grime of this city. Her face, though, that's something I don't need the rain to clean. Raw. Torn up. She's standing there, under the flicker of a dim streetlight, staring at the stump of what was once a young tree. A tree she planted, she tells me. Says she used to climb it, talk to it. Says it was a part of her. I nod, lean in, listen. The way she describes it, you'd think it was a living memory, one that kept her through the nights. Now it's just a story. And stories, they can't be cut down. Not as easy, anyway. I tell her that. Tell her she still has the roots, deep down where the saw can't reach. And maybe, just maybe, there's a new shoot waiting to poke through the soil.
